name: Jugol (Walled Old City)
tagline: The living labyrinth behind the ancient walls
description: The historic heart of Harar, a UNESCO-listed maze of narrow alleys ringed by ancient walls with five historic gates. Home to dozens of mosques, shrines, and brightly painted Harari houses, it is best explored slowly on foot with a guide who can read its culture and lanes.
pros: Painted houses and dozens of shrines
cons: Easy to get lost without a guide
Very basic infrastructure and weak wifi

name: Gidir Magala (Market Area)
description: The main market district inside Jugol, a bustling hub of spices, produce, textiles, and daily Harari life that has traded for generations. It is loud, colorful, and dense, the best place to feel the city's commercial pulse and to sample local coffee and street food among the crowds.
pros: Cheap food and famous Harari coffee

name: Rimbaud House & Modern Town
tagline: Museums and services outside the walls
description: The area around the ornate Rimbaud House museum and the newer town spreading beyond Jugol's gates. Here you find more hotels, cafes, banks, and everyday services, plus a slightly easier pace than the packed old city, making it a practical base with quick access to the walls.
bestFor: Travelers wanting more amenities and comfort

name: Dire Dawa (Transport Base)
tagline: The nearest airport and rail gateway
description: A larger, flatter, and warmer city about an hour from Harar down the escarpment, home to the nearest airport and a rail link toward Addis Ababa. Many travelers pass through or overnight here for flights and connections, using it as the practical transport hub for the region.
pros: Rail and road links to Addis Ababa
